claim: Diagnoses are exactly the minimal hitting sets of the minimal conflict sets (Reiter's theorem); a suspect set is valid only if it touches every contradiction found so far and no smaller subset does.
agent_test: Give the agent a toy fault task with known conflicts; compare plain 'name the culprit' with an explicit 'list contradictions, then smallest set touching all' step at equal tokens; score exact-diagnosis match.

claim: Reiter's original pruned breadth-first tree is incomplete: when a later, smaller conflict arrives, the closing and relabel rules interact and a minimal hitting set (e.g. {a,b} for {{a,b},{b,c},{a,c},{b,d},{b}}) is lost. HS-DAG (node reuse plus relabelling) repairs it.
schema_part: G (re-check pruned suspects when a conflict shrinks)/O (revise)
agent_test: Feed the agent conflict lists where a later conflict is a subset of an earlier one; count how often it drops a valid suspect set that was pruned early, with and without a 'reopen pruned suspects when a conflict shrinks' rule.

claim: The bug only bites when conflicts are non-minimal, i.e. the conflict finder returns a superset of a conflict seen earlier. LLM-produced contradictions are often non-minimal, so this boundary condition is probably the normal case for our agent (inference, not measured).
agent_test: Add a step that shrinks each stated contradiction to a minimal subset (drop one member, re-check) before using it; compare final diagnosis accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: No algorithm wins everywhere on pure hitting-set speed: GDE is best to about 30 components, Boolean algorithms lead beyond that (more than 10x over GDE), HS-DAG and HST are mid-pack, and HST can scale worse than HS-DAG above about 20 components.
agent_test: Not an agent question; relevant only to choosing a lightweight suspect enumerator in tool code.

claim: HST beats HS-DAG when only single-element hitting sets are wanted, but HS-DAG wins most of the range when sets up to size 3 are wanted; Wotawa's fix does not dominate Greiner's.
agent_test: None; implementation-dependent (Python, 300 s, 2 GiB).

claim: Across a benchmark of about two dozen minimal-hitting-set algorithms, specialised enumerators (MMCS, RS, HTC-BDD) are far faster than Reiter-style trees; HTC-BDD is 4 to 10x faster than rivals but often exhausts 32 GB.
agent_test: None for the agent; confirms tree search is a control idea, not a speed idea. Inputs were biology and data-mining sets, not diagnosis.

claim: The count of minimal hitting sets can explode (HER2+.SHORT: 122 elements, 534 sets, 128,833,310 minimal hitting sets, only 26,436 of size 7 or less), and deciding whether a hitting set of a given size exists is NP-complete, so a size cap (depth limit) is the standard control.
agent_test: Cap suspect-set size at 1, 2, 3 in the prompt and compare to unbounded listing at equal tokens; measure recall of the true fault and tokens wasted.

claim: Keeping the tree across measurements (DynamicHS) instead of rebuilding after each test gives the same diagnoses with a median 52% runtime saving, faster in 99.4% of scenarios (96% of single sessions); the 2019 pilot reported 59% fewer reasoner calls and 42% less time. All from one author group on ontology debugging.
agent_test: Compare an agent that restates and recomputes the suspect list after each probe result with one that carries and edits the list; same tokens, count turns to correct fault.

claim: DynamicHS is not uniformly better: median runtime was 2% to 3% worse in two scenarios, HS-Tree needed 76% less time in one scenario; absolute losses stayed at most 12 s.
agent_test: Report win rate, not just mean, when testing carried-state vs rebuild.

claim: Reiter's HS-Tree needs exponential space; recursive best-first search (RBF-HS) keeps soundness and best-first order in linear space, saving up to 98% memory (HS-Tree used up to 4900% more) with equal or lower runtime in 40% of cases.
agent_test: Analogue: keep only the top-k open suspects in context rather than the whole frontier; compare to full frontier at equal tokens.

claim: Best-first order with fault probabilities needs each component probability below 0.5 (or rescaling) for HS-Tree to stay sound (return only minimal diagnoses).
agent_test: If the agent weights suspects by prior, test that it does not report non-minimal sets when priors are high.

claim: Getting several conflicts per prover call (MergeXplain) speeds diagnosis 15% to 54% on harder problems but loses 5% to 11% when only one conflict exists; breadth-first HS-DAG predicted the user's preferred diagnosis worst while FastDiag found a preferred minimal diagnosis directly.
agent_test: Ask the agent for several independent contradictions per step versus one per step; compare tokens to first correct diagnosis. Expect gain only when many conflicts exist.

claim: Direct diagnosis computation without precomputing conflicts (Inv-HS-Tree, SAT encodings) beats conflict-then-hit when conflicts are many: in 13 hard ontology cases HS-Tree could not find the requested diagnoses in 2 hours; SATbD solved 99.3% of c7552 observations in 30 s. These are strong rivals to tree search.
agent_test: Compare 'find contradictions then hit' with 'guess a candidate and test it' as agent strategies at equal tokens.

claim: Narrowing diagnoses by chosen tests (sequential diagnosis) works best with entropy or split rules; entropy beat split-in-half in ontology debugging; ENT, SPL and MPS gave similar runtime savings (50/52/52%).
agent_test: Have the agent pick the probe that splits current suspects most evenly versus a free choice; compare probes to resolution.

claim: LLMs given the conflict-then-diagnosis pipeline with pseudo-code on small circuits: o3-mini F1 0.917 (conflicts) and 0.784 (diagnoses); diagnosis quality falls as relations and diagnoses grow (up to 165); non-reasoning models near zero on unseen examples; authors conclude LLMs are no alternative to diagnosis algorithms.
schema_part: S5/G (offload exact hitting to a tool)
agent_test: Replicate on our agent with 3 to 8 conflicts: LLM-only hitting set vs LLM writes conflicts and a code tool computes minimal hitting sets. Measure F1 at equal tokens.

claim: Domain knowledge in the prompt did not help MSO/conflict generation, the easy incidence-matrix step is solved perfectly by reasoning models, and conflict scores look better on bigger examples only because zero-conflict cases score badly (empty-vs-empty convention).
agent_test: Check our scorer for the empty-set edge case before any comparison.

claim: Plain LLMs diagnosing small circuits and heating systems from text: best hit rate 79.5% (Gemini 2.5 Flash), 76.9% Mistral Large, 25.6% best small model; hallucination 20.5% for the best versus most small models above 70%.
agent_test: Add a guardrail that every named suspect must be a listed component; measure hallucination rate with and without.

claim: LLMs are weak at the conflict-detection side: they label almost every formula satisfiable and miss the phase transition (3-SAT, over 2700 formulas), which suggests missed contradictions in the agent's own conflict step.
agent_test: Seed tasks with a hidden contradiction vs none; measure the false 'consistent' rate of the agent.

claim: LLM root-cause agents on real telemetry fail often: OpenRCA best accuracy 11.34%, a 1675-run study perfect accuracy 3.9% to 12.5%, symptom-as-cause in 39.9% of runs; hypothesis-driven prompting widened coverage but did not stop interpretation errors; OpenRCA 2.0 exact root-cause-set match 20.7%.
agent_test: Add an 'is this a symptom or a cause?' check per suspect; compare symptom-as-cause rate at equal tokens.

claim: A ReAct agent with retrieval cut hallucination (4% vs 12% for CoT) at similar correctness (35% vs 39%) on cloud incidents, but returns one answer, not a set.
agent_test: Report hallucination separately from correctness.

claim: No 2020-2026 study was found that puts an LLM inside a Reiter HS-tree or tests LLMs on HS-DAG non-minimal-conflict handling; closest is the DX 2025 pipeline study. Search was rate-limited, so this is a gap, not proof. Gap search 2026-11-03 (limited by rate-limited APIs) again found none.
agent_test: Run our own test: the K02 counterexample as a prompt, see whether the agent keeps {a,b}.

claim: Hybrid designs where a solver does the exact minimal-set work and the LLM only verbalises or proposes (Delta1, SafeMin) exist, but evidence is demonstration-level or snippet-only.
agent_test: Same as K15 with a tool arm.

claim: Recent LLM failure-attribution work for multi-agent systems (AgentLocate, Famas) does not use a hitting-set formulation. AgentLocate uses propose-then-verify on one suspect; Famas ranks steps by spectrum suspiciousness across repeated runs.
agent_test: Compare 'one named suspect, three independent checks' with 'full suspect list plus hitting set' on the same failed traces.

claim: Independent re-checks of a leading hypothesis help up to about three checks: agent-level accuracy 35.71% to 69.05% from 1 to 3 evaluators, no consistent gain at 5 or 7 (Qwen-7B, small test set).
agent_test: Cap independent re-checks of the top suspect at 3 in a budgeted run and test whether more help.

claim: Repeated-run suspiciousness scoring (spectrum analysis) beat LLM-only judges at action level on Who&When (29.35% vs about 19.7% for the best LLM method) but action accuracy is still below 30%.
agent_test: Count a suspect's appearance across passing and failing attempts in code instead of asking the LLM to judge.

claim: At equal tokens, no study compares an LLM doing the exact minimal-hitting-set step in-context against a code tool. The one tool data point (gpt-4o-mini with interpreter) was worst, but it was also the weakest model; LLM diagnosis F1 falls as diagnoses grow even with gold conflicts.
agent_test: Run both arms on generated conflict families of growing size, same token cap, score exact minimal diagnoses.

claim: Choosing the next probe by splitting the candidate set near 50/50, with set sizes counted outside the LLM, improves LLM question-asking: +38.1% mean success over direct prompting (UoT), 97.0% on DX, 67.3% vs 43.7% troubleshooting. The exact reward form matters little (plain IG within 1 to 3 points of variants).
agent_test: Compare 'halve the suspects' with 'most likely suspect first' for the next test, at equal question budget.

claim: No study varies the fault-size cap (single, double, triple fault) for LLM agents. RCA studies assume a single fault; the one that checks admits multi-cause cases are harder and untested.
agent_test: Generate tasks with 1, 2 and 3 simultaneous faults; compare agent accuracy with and without a stated size cap.

claim: Anchoring, repetition and failure to update belief are the reasoning failures that predict wrong LLM root-cause answers; they are the same behaviours a reopen-pruned-suspects rule targets, but that rule itself has not been tested.
agent_test: Seed a run with a late smaller contradiction and count whether the agent revives a pruned suspect.
